svg.title: Privately educated people are over-represented in 42 of 46 elite groups
svg.desc: Stacked bars: share of each of 46 elite groups who mostly attended a private, grammar or comprehensive secondary school, or were schooled abroad, from the Sutton Trust's Elitist Britain 2025, sorted by the private share; the population benchmark is 7% private. Senior military officers: private 63%, grammar 18%, comprehensive 16%; Senior judges: private 62%, grammar 15%, comprehensive 21%; Cricketers (men): private 59%, grammar 0%, comprehensive 32%; Sunday Times Young Power List: private 54%, grammar 7%, comprehensive 37%; Diplomats: private 53%, grammar 17%, comprehensive 28%; House of Lords: private 52%, grammar 20%, comprehensive 23%; Shadow cabinet: private 52%, grammar 12%, comprehensive 32%; Newspaper columnists: private 50%, grammar 15%, comprehensive 18%; Cricketers (women): private 50%, grammar 4%, comprehensive 46%; Permanent secretaries: private 47%, grammar 18%, comprehensive 29%; FTSE 100 chairs: private 47%, grammar 14%, comprehensive 9%; Political commentators: private 47%, grammar 13%, comprehensive 33%; Property owners and landowners: private 46%, grammar 6%, comprehensive 27%; Podcasters: private 45%, grammar 4%, comprehensive 43%; PR consultancy CEOs: private 43%, grammar 16%, comprehensive 32%; Shadow junior ministers: private 41%, grammar 21%, comprehensive 36%; BBC executives: private 38%, grammar 14%, comprehensive 29%; Rugby players (men): private 36%, grammar 4%, comprehensive 49%; Charity CEOs: private 34%, grammar 15%, comprehensive 42%; News media 100: private 33%, grammar 10%, comprehensive 48%; Olympic medallists (2024): private 33%, grammar 8%, comprehensive 52%; Film and TV actors: private 32%, grammar 9%, comprehensive 41%; Journalists: private 30%, grammar 9%, comprehensive 54%; Public body CEOs: private 28%, grammar 17%, comprehensive 45%; Entrepreneurs: private 27%, grammar 9%, comprehensive 26%; Sunday Times Rich List: private 27%, grammar 6%, comprehensive 16%; Tech firm CEOs: private 26%, grammar 9%, comprehensive 23%; Think-tank leaders: private 25%, grammar 10%, comprehensive 53%; MPs: private 24%, grammar 12%, comprehensive 62%; Junior ministers: private 23%, grammar 12%, comprehensive 63%; Police chiefs and commissioners: private 21%, grammar 19%, comprehensive 60%; Scottish Parliament: private 21%, grammar 0%, comprehensive 74%; Special advisers: private 20%, grammar 20%, comprehensive 55%; Paralympic medallists (2024): private 20%, grammar 4%, comprehensive 73%; FTSE 100 chief executives: private 18%, grammar 14%, comprehensive 16%; Influencers and content creators: private 18%, grammar 10%, comprehensive 68%; University vice-chancellors: private 15%, grammar 13%, comprehensive 50%; Senedd Cymru: private 14%, grammar 8%, comprehensive 78%; Trade union leaders: private 12%, grammar 9%, comprehensive 76%; Local government leaders: private 10%, grammar 16%, comprehensive 74%; Pop stars: private 10%, grammar 10%, comprehensive 76%; Rugby players (women): private 9%, grammar 1%, comprehensive 80%; Cabinet: private 7%, grammar 7%, comprehensive 86%; Footballers (men): private 5%, grammar 1%, comprehensive 93%; Footballers (women): private 4%, grammar 5%, comprehensive 85%; Northern Ireland Assembly: private 0%, grammar 62%, comprehensive 37%.
svg.text: Privately educated people are over-represented in 42 of 46 elite groups
School where each person spent most of their secondary education, % of each group (Sutton Trust, Elitist Britain 2025)
Dashed line: 7% of people went to private school. Comprehensive includes secondary moderns; direct-grant grammars count as private
